problem: The company wanted a refreshed look for the brand.
title: Tropicana redesigns its carton, sees sales fall, and returns to the old design
context: PepsiCo launched new cartons for Tropicana Pure Premium on 8 January 2009.
decision_made: Replace the familiar orange-with-straw carton with a new design.
action_taken: Announced on 23 February 2009 that it would scrap the new design.
observed_outcome: Unit sales reportedly fell 20 percent and dollar sales 19 percent between 1 January and 22 February 2009. The company said it had underestimated the emotional bond customers had with the old carton.
lessons: Customers can be strongly attached to a recognisable package, and a redesign can cost real sales before it is tested widely.
limitations: Sales data was reported via trade press from retail tracking data. Cost estimates range from about $27 million to $50 million and include different items. Competitors' gains were reported by AOL.

claims.claim_text: PepsiCo launched new Tropicana Pure Premium cartons in January 2009 and scrapped them in February.
Unit sales fell about 20 percent in the weeks after the redesign, according to retail tracking data.
